context.problemStatement:
Implement the `Lambda` case of `eval`. An anonymous function `fn(x) { ... }`
evaluates to a function value. Nothing in its body is evaluated until it is
called, so this case never returns an error. Build a `VFunc(UserFn(...))` whose
name is `"lambda"` (used in error messages) and whose parent is the environment
in which this function was *defined*, not the one in which it will be called. This
is what lets a function use the names around it, even after the call that created it
has returned.

```
// In eval:
    Lambda(params, body) ->
      // YOUR CODE HERE (replace the code below)
      Error(errors.NotImplemented(
        "Lambda("
        <> string.inspect(params)
        <> ", "
        <> string.inspect(body)
        <> ")",
      ))
```

Run the tests:

```
gleam test -- q8
```

targets.claim: Student can explain why their Lambda case never returns an error even when the body of the anonymous function uses an unbound name, and when such an error would appear instead.

probes.question: In your `Lambda(params, body)` case, why does evaluating an anonymous function containing an unbound variable not return an error immediately, and when would that unbound variable error actually happen?
probes.reason: Directly asks the student to explain why the Lambda case returns Ok without evaluating the body, and at what point any runtime errors in the body are triggered.

probes.question: If `body` in `Lambda(params, body)` contains an undefined variable like `undefined_var`, why does your code successfully return `Ok(VFunc(...))` instead of an `Error`, and at what point in program execution would that error arise?
probes.reason: Uses a concrete example of an unbound variable to test whether the student understands that definition-time does not evaluate the body while call-time does.

content: In your `Lambda(params, body)` case, why does evaluating an anonymous function containing an unbound variable not return an error immediately, and when would that unbound variable error actually happen?

The body of a lambda function is not evaluated until the lambda function is called, we when we lookup the unbound variable in current frame and parent frames of the lambda function and fail to find it, we will get an unbound variable error

reason: The student correctly explained both parts: the body is not evaluated until the lambda is called, and the unbound variable error happens during evaluation upon call when looking up the name across the frames.
